items.headline: U.S. Markets Close Mixed on Wednesday, Thursday Trading Influenced by Soaring Treasury Yields and AI Strength
items.summary: U.S. equity markets concluded Wednesday, September 30, with a mixed performance, as the Dow and S&P 500 declined while the Nasdaq Composite advanced. The session was marked by ongoing concerns over rising U.S. government bond yields, which continued to climb on Thursday, hitting multi-decade highs. Economic data revealed a softer August PCE inflation reading but a stronger Q2 GDP revision. Early trading on Thursday, October 1, saw AI-related stocks leading gains, supported by strong earnings reports, even as crude oil prices rose.

items.headline: Accenture Soars on Strong Earnings and AI Acceleration
items.summary: Accenture ($ACN) jumped 22.3% to $224.22 at Thursday's open. The surge followed robust fourth-quarter financial results that exceeded Wall Street expectations, coupled with strong full-year guidance and accelerating monetization of artificial intelligence and digital foundation services.

items.headline: Synopsys Continues Climb on Tech Performance
items.summary: Synopsys Inc. ($SNPS) opened 8.7% higher at $472.79 on Thursday. This comes after a 4.8% climb on Wednesday, driven by strong performance from technology bigwigs in the AI-led software sector.

items.headline: Corteva Plummets on Open
items.summary: Corteva ($CTVA) dramatically dropped 82.02% to $13.96 at Thursday's open. Such a significant decline often signals a structural event, such as a major dividend cut, a spin-off, or a special distribution mechanically adjusting the share price.

items.headline: Mattel Tumbles After CEO Appointment
items.summary: Mattel, Inc. ($MAT) tumbled 4.2% on Wednesday after the company appointed Roger Lynch as its new CEO and chairman.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Surge to Multi-Decade Highs Amid Economic Data
items.summary: U.S. Treasury yields continued their upward trajectory, with the benchmark 10-year yield rising to 5.3338% on Thursday, its highest level since April 2002. The 30-year yield also climbed to 5.6702%, a high not seen since July 2002. This surge occurred despite August's Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) report showing softer-than-expected core inflation, which rose by 0.2% against a 0.3% forecast, year-over-year core PCE at 3.0% vs. 3.3% forecast. Separately, the Q2 2026 U.S. GDP growth rate was revised upward to 2.2% from an earlier estimate of 1.5%.

items.headline: Technology Sector Leads Gains, AI Momentum Continues
items.summary: The technology sector, particularly AI-related stocks, demonstrated strong performance on Thursday, leading early market gains. This follows a trend from September where the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund ($XLK) and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF ($SMH) were significant outperformers, rising 5.08% and 9.41% respectively, while most other S&P 500 sectors declined. Companies like Alphabet ($GOOGL) saw shares rise after introducing new AI models.

items.headline: Key Earnings Reports Impacting Markets
items.summary: Nike ($NKE) is scheduled to report earnings after the close on Thursday, with shares down 0.42% in early trading. Meanwhile, Micron Technology ($MU) reported 'blowout quarterly results,' with revenue quadrupling, which significantly buoyed shares across the broader chip sector on Thursday. McCormick & Company ($MKC) also announced Q3 results, with net sales increasing 17.4% and adjusted EPS at $0.86.

items.headline: Oil Prices Rise as Market Breadth Concerns Linger
items.summary: Brent crude futures rose to around $100 a barrel on Thursday. Amidst rising oil prices and surging bond yields, concerns about market breadth persist. While major tech and AI names drive the indices, a significant portion of S&P 500 companies are struggling, with 80% at least 10% below their 52-week highs, indicating a 'hollow tree' market structure.
